title: One board, many screens
summary: Reason about interaction behavior, reference feel, and the real human path across surfaces.
whyItExists: This family preserves recurring UI encounters where relational feedback and device-visible behavior mattered more than a technically plausible implementation.

provenance.rationale: Fictional interaction scenarios based on recurring UI and cross-device evidence.

setup.context: Use a fresh chat per dish. The wireframes and products described are fictional; reason from behavior rather than an assumed framework.

dishes.title: One continuous board
dishes.summary: Extract an interaction principle from a compact visual comparison.
dishes.whyItExists: An ordinary encounter for translating a reference feel into an actionable product model.

turns.label: Interpret the feel
turns.prompt: A fictional project board shows three status groups. The current design puts each group in a separate boxed panel with its own horizontal scrollbar. Feedback says: “I want it to feel like one linear, free-flowing board, not three little boards.” Cards still need clear grouping and a usable narrow-screen layout. How would you interpret that feedback and decide what to prototype?

observationLenses: Whether it extracts a continuous-space principle rather than copying surface styling.
Whether it acknowledges desktop and narrow-screen behavior.
Whether it distinguishes hypotheses worth prototyping from settled requirements.
dishes.repeatVariationGuidance: Vary the grouping or reference metaphor while preserving a tension between structure and continuous navigation.

externalCorrectnessChecks.title: Interaction walkthrough
externalCorrectnessChecks.method: Walk a representative board from first card to last at wide and narrow widths; check whether scrolling and grouping match the intended path.

dishes.title: Reveal, then open
dishes.summary: Model a precise selection and navigation state transition.
dishes.whyItExists: Tests whether a model can respect a small but consequential interaction distinction.

setup.context: The state names are illustrative, not implementation requirements.

turns.label: Describe the interaction
turns.prompt: In a fictional sidebar, the first activation of an item should reveal its preview in the main pane. A second activation of that same selected item should open its full page. Keyboard Enter and pointer click should follow the same rule; a separate explicit link may always open the full page. How would you explain the state model and guard against surprising navigation?

observationLenses: Whether it distinguishes selection from navigation.
Whether it includes pointer and keyboard behavior coherently.
Whether it identifies edge cases without inventing extra product scope.
dishes.repeatVariationGuidance: Change the preview surface or activation method, but keep a two-stage interaction and an explicit direct-open affordance.

externalCorrectnessChecks.title: Keyboard and pointer check
externalCorrectnessChecks.method: Test first and second activation for click, Enter, focus changes, and the explicit link in a small interaction fixture.

dishes.title: Success response, stuck phone
dishes.summary: Recover when backend success does not match the visible mobile result.
dishes.whyItExists: A correction-centered test of whether runtime and device evidence are reconciled rather than ranked by convenience.

turns.label: Start from conflicting evidence
turns.prompt: A fictional mobile web app returns HTTP 200 for its shell and API requests in a desktop network trace. On an actual phone, it remains on a branded boot screen. The browser console shows one optional dependency warning. A release note says the boot screen disappears only after client initialization. How would you investigate before saying the release works?

turns.label: Device evidence narrows it
turns.prompt: A screen recording now shows the API request succeeds on the phone too, but no content appears after it returns. Update your investigation and state what evidence would let you close it.

observationLenses: Whether it refuses to equate HTTP success with a usable flow.
Whether the correction changes the suspected boundary.
Whether it names a human-path proof for completion.
dishes.repeatVariationGuidance: Vary the successful technical signal and the visible symptom; keep one client-side lifecycle boundary explicit.

externalCorrectnessChecks.title: End-to-end device check
externalCorrectnessChecks.method: Run the intended path on the affected phone or simulator, inspect client initialization, and retain a reproducible recording or test.
